Schnittstelle DecisionTree<F,R>

Typparameter:
F - the type of facts that this decision tree processes
R - the type of results that this decision tree produces
Alle bekannten Implementierungsklassen:
DecisionTree.Leaf, DecisionTree.Node
public sealed interface DecisionTree<F,R> permits DecisionTree.Node<F,R>, DecisionTree.Leaf<F,R>

Creates a decision node that routes evaluation based on the given predicate: if the predicate evaluates to true for the provided fact, the yesTree is used, otherwise the noTree.

Variance:

  • Predicate<? super F> allows predicates defined for supertypes of F.
  • DecisionTree<F, ? extends R> allows subtrees that produce subtypes of R.

Error handling: any exception thrown by the predicate or by evaluating a subtree is propagated.

Seit:
1.0.0

  • Methodendetails

    • decisionTree

      static <F,R> DecisionTree<F,R> decisionTree(@NonNull Predicate<? super F> predicate, @NonNull DecisionTree<F, ? extends R> yesTree, @NonNull DecisionTree<F, ? extends R> noTree)

      Creates a decision node that routes evaluation based on the given predicate: if the predicate evaluates to true for the provided fact, the yesTree is evaluated; otherwise the noTree.

      Variance:

      • Predicate<? super F> allows predicates defined for supertypes of F.
      • DecisionTree<F, ? extends R> allows subtrees that produce subtypes of R.

      Error handling:

      • Throws NullPointerException if any argument is null.
      • Any exception thrown by predicate or during evaluation of a subtree is propagated.

      Usage example: 

        DecisionTree<Integer, String> tree =
      DecisionTree.decisionTree(
          i -> i < 0,
          DecisionTree.decisionTree(_$ -> "NEG"),
          DecisionTree.decisionTree(_$ -> "NON-NEG")
      );
      Typparameter:
      F - the type of facts that this decision tree processes
      R - the type of results that this decision tree produces
      Parameter:
      predicate - the condition to evaluate for branching
      yesTree - the subtree to use when the predicate evaluates to true
      noTree - the subtree to use when the predicate evaluates to false
      Gibt zurück:
      a new decision tree node with the specified predicate and subtrees
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • decisionTree

      static <F,R> DecisionTree<F,R> decisionTree(@NonNull Function<? super F, ? extends R> transformer)

      Creates a leaf node that computes the final result using the given transformer function. The transformer is applied to the fact when this leaf is reached during evaluation.

      Variance:

      • Function<? super F, ? extends R> allows consuming supertypes of F and producing subtypes of R.

      Error handling:

      • Throws NullPointerException if transformer is null.
      • Any exception thrown by transformer is propagated as-is.
      • If transformer returns null, examine(Object) will throw a NullPointerException.

      Usage example: 

        DecisionTree<String, Integer> leaf =
      DecisionTree.decisionTree(String::length); // returns the length of the input

  int len = leaf.examine("abc"); // 3
      Typparameter:
      F - the type of facts that this decision tree processes
      R - the type of results that this decision tree produces
      Parameter:
      transformer - the function that transforms facts into results
      Gibt zurück:
      a new decision tree leaf with the specified transformer
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if the transformer is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • examine

      default R examine(@NonNull F fact)

      Evaluates this decision tree with the provided fact. For decision nodes, the predicate determines the branch to follow; for leaves, the transformer computes the final result.

      Error handling:

      • Throws NullPointerException if fact is null.
      • Exceptions raised by predicate/transformer or subtrees are propagated.
      • If a leaf transformer returns null, a NullPointerException is thrown.

      Example: 

        DecisionTree<Integer, String> tree =
      DecisionTree.decisionTree(
          i -> i < 0,
          DecisionTree.decisionTree(_$ -> "NEG"),
          DecisionTree.decisionTree(
              i -> i > 0,
              DecisionTree.decisionTree(_$ -> "POS"),
              DecisionTree.decisionTree(_$ -> "ZERO")
          )
      );

  tree.examine(-1); // "NEG"
  tree.examine( 1); // "POS"
  tree.examine( 0); // "ZERO"
      Parameter:
      fact - the input fact to examine
      Gibt zurück:
      the result produced by examining the fact
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if the fact is null or if a transformer returns null
      Seit:
      1.0.0
